title: Targeted connection fence and ephemeral priority trimmer for softer regional drains
author: Maya Li
release_notes: Introduce a soft-park connection fence and tenant-aware ephemeral priority trimmer to reduce reopen storms during KV drains and regional probes. Canaried in eu-west-1 behind feature flag.
description: Summary: Patch to reduce noisy cross-region circuit flips by introducing a targeted connection fence for in-flight KV drains and an ephemeral priority trimmer that reduces per-tenant concurrency during imminent regional failovers. Motivation: Recent incident INC-2026 showed cascaded reopen storms when nodes drained KV cache while regional probes jittered; this PR aims for minimal-impact throttling to keep SLOs stable. Implementation: add connection_fence with graceful-park state, pre-drain marker annotations for active sessions, ephemeral priority_trimmer that reduces admission for low-priority tenants by percent-based windowed backoff, and a soft-promote path that re-evaluates priorities after health stabilization. Also add new telemetry (fence_state transitions, trimmer actions, tenant-level preemptions), trace spans for fence lifecycle, and feature flag redwood.experimental.soft_drain_fence. Tests: unit tests for fence state machine, integration test simulating KV drain + probe jitter, e2e canary harness script. Rollout plan: enable in eu-west-1 for low-impact tenant cohort, monitor SLO delta and per-tenant error budget consumption for 72 hours, gradually expand with automated rollback if SLO regressions exceed threshold. Related work: ENG-3921, ENG-4008. CLI: added devtool command devtool drain-fence inspect to view fence state for a region.

Samir Gupta (reviewer): Integration run failed once due to flaky network emulator (CI job 4123). Rerun after adding a small jitter tolerance to the test harness. Maya: adjusted harness and re-ran; CI green (job 4125).
